text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Workup for suspected inflammatory bowel disease: blood count, CRP, albumin, iron studies, vitamin B12 and D, fecal calprotectin, stool tests for Clostridioides difficile and enteric pathogens, celiac serology, a pregnancy test, ileocolonoscopy with biopsies, and MR enterography
  • Exclude intestinal tuberculosis before any steroid or immunosuppressive drug: interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and ileal and colonic biopsies for acid-fast stain, TB PCR, and mycobacterial culture; with hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, measles, and varicella serology before treatment
  • Gastroenterology (inflammatory bowel disease) consultation once the endoscopy and imaging are done, to confirm the diagnosis and choose treatment with her
  • Nutrition: dietitian assessment, small frequent meals with oral nutritional supplements, and weight at every visit
  • Mood, anxiety, and work: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intervals, IBD psychology if needed, and a practical plan for composing and performing during treatment
  • Risankizumab 600 mg intravenously at weeks 0, 4, and 8, then 360 mg subcutaneously every 8 weeks, chosen with her as early advanced therapy; liver enzymes and bilirubin at baseline and through at least week 12; a short prednisone bridge tapered over eight weeks; no live vaccines
  • Vaccines before immunosuppression: PCV20, recombinant zoster vaccine in two doses, a hepatitis B booster with an antibody check one to two months later, and influenza and COVID-19 vaccines each season; live vaccines not needed because she is immune to measles and varicella
  • Iron, vitamin D, and bone: one intravenous ferric derisomaltose infusion, vitamin D3 daily, calcium while on prednisone, baseline DXA, and weight-bearing exercise
  • Treat to target: symptoms and CRP at every visit, fecal calprotectin at about three and six months, and ileocolonoscopy at six to twelve months
  • Contraception, fertility, and pregnancy planning: effective contraception while the disease is active; plan pregnancy after three to six months of steroid-free remission, with a preconception review; continue the biologic in pregnancy after discussing the limited data for risankizumab; folic acid before conception

resource.title: Lili Boulanger synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss in a young woman of 21: confirm Crohn disease by ileocolonoscopy with biopsies and MR enterography, and exclude intestinal tuberculosis before any immunosuppression (interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and biopsies for acid-fast bacilli, TB PCR, and culture); classify the disease (Montreal) and its risk; start an advanced therapy early for moderate to severe disease, with latent tuberculosis, hepatitis B, and vaccine preparation first; correct iron, vitamin D, and nutrition; protect bone; treat to target with CRP, fecal calprotectin, and endoscopy; plan contraception, fertility, and pregnancy; screen mood; and help her keep composing. The historical illness is graded R: called intestinal tuberculosis in her time and proposed to be Crohn disease since, it is not settled.
